costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Jaguar AJ133 engine typically takes 14-18 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent specialist) due to the tight engine bay packaging and the complexity of the supercharger and cooling ancillaries .

failures.title: Jaguar AJ133 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - 2009-2012 models
items.whatHappens: Early AJ133 engines used hydraulic timing chain tensioners that were prone to premature wear and loss of oil pressure. This leads to chain slack, a distinct rattling noise on cold starts, and in severe cases, chain jump causing catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: While a tensioner and chain replacement is possible, the labour intensity of accessing the front covers on this V8 often makes a full reconditioned Jaguar AJ133 engine replacement the more reliable and financially sensible option if the engine has already suffered timing-related damage.

items.title: Supercharger Coupler Degradation - All AJ133 variants
items.whatHappens: The supercharger is driven by a rubber/plastic isolator coupler that wears out over time. Symptoms include a loud rattling or whining noise from the front of the engine, particularly at idle or low RPM, which may temporarily disappear as the engine warms up.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the coupler is a standard repair and does not require a full engine replacement. However, if the noise is ignored for too long, metal debris can enter the supercharger or oil system, escalating the repair scope significantly.

items.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe Leaks - All AJ133 variants
items.whatHappens: Plastic coolant crossover pipes located in the valley of the V8 become brittle after years of heat cycling. They develop micro-cracks, leading to slow coolant loss, sweet-smelling steam from the engine bay, and potential overheating if not addressed.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the crossover pipes is a straightforward preventative repair. If ignored, overheating can warp the cylinder heads, necessitating a full engine replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2013 Jaguar AJ133 engines received revised, more robust timing chain tensioners and updated cooling components, making them significantly more reliable and far less prone to catastrophic timing failures than the early 2009-2012 examples .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJ133
variants.intro: As a Specific page type, this section focuses on accurate identification and avoiding common, costly misidentifications. The AJ133 engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the front of the cylinder block and is also recorded on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Number". Owners frequently confuse the AJ133 with the naturally aspirated 5.0L variant (badged internally as 508PN) or the smaller 3.0L supercharged V6 (AJ126). While the AJ133 and 508PN share the same 5.0-litre block architecture, the AJ133 features a Roots-type supercharger, different pistons, and a distinct engine management calibration. Fitting a naturally aspirated ECU or wiring loom to a supercharged AJ133 will result in incorrect fueling, severe knocking, and rapid engine destruction. Furthermore, the AJ133 is distinct from the older AJ-V8 4.2SC. The AJ133 features a new block design, direct injection (on later variants), and a different supercharger mounting configuration, meaning they are not interchangeable without extensive chassis and wiring modifications.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ133 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Jaguar AJ133 engine for sale can be a budget-friendly option for early XKR or XF models, but only if the seller can provide documented proof that the timing chain tensioners have been updated to the post-2013 specification. Without this history, the risk of inheriting a pre-failure timing assembly is high. Learn more about used engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: For most owners, a reconditioned Jaguar AJ133 is the optimal choice. A proper recon will proactively address the engine’s known weaknesses by fitting revised timing chain tensioners, replacing the supercharger coupler, and installing updated metal coolant crossover pipes, delivering near-new reliability for high-performance driving. Explore reconditioned engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for concours-restoration XKR-S or F-Type SVR projects where the engine is being stripped to the bare block. This allows for line-boring the main bearings, balancing the rotating assembly, and porting the cylinder heads to ensure the engine matches the pristine, high-output specification of the restored chassis. View rebuilt engine services.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting your replacement through our vetted network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with Jaguar's complex supercharger and cooling systems, backed by a nationwide warranty. Check supply and fit availability.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Classic and modern-performance Jaguar models (XK, XJ, F-Type) typically hold values between £8,000 and £35,000, depending on mileage, specification, and condition . Because a fully reconditioned Jaguar AJ133 engine replacement can approach £9,000, it is crucial to evaluate the vehicle's overall condition before committing. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value first.

items.question: How much does a Jaguar AJ133 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Jaguar AJ133 engine typically costs between £5,500 and £9,000 for supply only, with fitted prices ranging from £6,410 to £10,170. Used units start around £3,000 but carry a high risk of inherited timing chain or supercharger issues. Full rebuilt units for high-performance F-Type or XKR applications can exceed £12,000. Labour typically adds 14-18 hours at £65-£85/hr for an independent specialist.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jaguar AJ133 engine?
items.answer: The most critical failure on early (2009-2012) AJ133 engines is timing chain tensioner wear, which can lead to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact. Supercharger coupler degradation is also highly prevalent, causing a distinct rattling noise at idle. Plastic coolant crossover pipes in the V8 valley become brittle and leak over time. Post-2013 models received revised tensioners and are significantly more robust.

items.question: Which Jaguar models use the AJ133 engine?
items.answer: The AJ133 5.0-litre supercharged V8 was fitted to the Jaguar XF, XJ, XK, and F-Type between 2009 and 2022. It served as the flagship performance engine for the XKR, XJR, and F-Type R/SVR models. Power outputs ranged from 470 hp in standard tunes to 575 hp in SVR applications. It replaced the older 4.2-litre supercharged V8 across the entire performance lineup.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ133 engine?
items.answer: For any supercharged Jaguar, a reconditioned AJ133 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the high cost of timing chain repairs. Used engines often inherit the pre-2013 tensioner flaws or worn supercharger couplers. A proper reconditioned build proactively installs the revised post-2013 timing components. Reconditioned units also include updated metal coolant pipes to prevent future overheating.

items.question: What is the difference between the AJ133 and the AJ126?
items.answer: The AJ133 is a 5.0-litre supercharged V8, while the AJ126 is a 3.0-litre supercharged V6 derived from the same basic architecture. The AJ126 essentially removes two cylinders from the AJ133 block but shares the same supercharger mounting and cooling layout. They are not interchangeable; the AJ126 requires different engine mounts, exhaust manifolds, and ECU calibration. Both engines share similar vulnerabilities regarding coolant crossover pipes and water pumps.
